document.title: System pro M compact — DIN Rail components for low voltage installation, Catalogue 2014

modelingNotes: Exact order is DS202C M C16 A30: two protected poles, C characteristic, 16 A, type A residual-current protection, 30 mA; Icn 10 kA under IEC/EN 61009.
Diagram markings are preserved literally: 1/2 and 3/4 at top; 2/1 and 4/3 at bottom. Each slash marking denotes one connection, not two pins. No fixed phase or neutral assignment is made.

Two mechanically linked breaker contacts are represented in the open state. Neither contact metadata nor the ganged relation creates net continuity. No permanent external-terminal links exist; T identifies the internal test mechanism, not an external terminal.

Complete base-device external connection inventory only; no separately ordered auxiliaries, releases, motor operator, PE, shield or communication connection is included. Cable and busbar entry are uses of the same terminal, not separate connector endpoints.

Generic breaker symbols cover both poles. Residual-current sensing, test resistor/button and protective trip response are documented, not simulated. No universally required external terminal is asserted; wiring suitability depends on the application.

ABB brochure 2CSC422004B0203, undated, p.9: 230 V AC, 50/60 Hz; test-button range 110–253 V. At 230 V AC under IEC/EN 60947-2, DS202C M Icu is 10 kA and Ics 7.5 kA; rated residual breaking capacity is 6 kA. These are distinct conditional ratings, not load-current limits. https://library.e.abb.com/public/57606be65add4edd9a1ddee0ad27d6ba/2CSC422004B0203.pdf

The model records 16 A and AC capability only; voltage and frequency conditions stay in notes. Historical brochure p.9 lists 25 mm² cable and 10 mm² busbar terminal capacity, 2.8 Nm tightening torque; p.3 specifies 25 mm² flexible cable. These are manufacturer limits, not conductor-sizing approval.

connectionCoverage.notes: Four base-device power terminals with original slash markings; internal test mechanism has no external terminal. No fitted auxiliary, PE, shield or communication connection. Trip/test behavior is not simulated.
